meta.title: Ch 15: Analysis of Financial Statements — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 15 (Analysis of Financial Statements).

questions.q: The Rs 20 crore FV rise on held bonds is shown:
o: In OCI (with EIR interest of 35 in P&L)
questions.why: Debt at FVOCI carries dual books: amortised cost drives interest/impairment in P&L; the difference to fair value sits in OCI.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: debt-at-FVOCI lives double EIR in P&L, swing in OCI — one bond, two ledgers.

questions.stem: Meridian Ltd (year end 31 March) holds govt bonds measured at FVOCI (hold-to-collect-and-sell): face Rs 500 crore, coupon 7% bought at par. At year end their FV is Rs 520 crore. During the year Meridian also sold earlier-recognized FVOCI bonds whose cumulative OCI gain was Rs 12 crore, and the 12-month ECL allowance on remaining debt rose by Rs 5 crore. Interest was received on 31 March.

questions.q: On selling the other bonds, the Rs 12 crore OCI gain is:
o: Recycled to P&L as a reclassification adjustment
questions.why: Debt FVOCI recycling on derecognition; equity FVOCI election would not recycle — the distinction the case hunts.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: recycle-for-debt, no-recycle-for-equity Debt's OCI has a return ticket; the equity election burns the passport.

questions.stem: Meridian Ltd (year end 31 March) holds govt bonds measured at FVOCI (hold-to-collect-and-sell): face Rs 500 crore, coupon 7% bought at par. At year end their FV is Rs 520 crore. Interest was received on 31 March.

questions.q: The Rs 5 crore ECL increase is presented as:
o: P&L impairment loss; cumulative allowance in OCI — B/S carrying stays at FV
questions.why: For FVOCI debt, the loss allowance is recognised in OCI (reducing the accumulated OCI amount) while the asset's balance-sheet carrying remains at FV; P&L takes the charge.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: the B/S-needs-no-help nuance Already at fair value — so impairment books expense and OCI, and the asset shrugs.

questions.q: Interest received Rs 35 crore can appear under Ind AS 7 as:
questions.why: Ind AS 7 permits interest received in operating or investing — consistency required.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: the allowed-slot questions Interest in can be O or I — one policy, every year.

questions.q: Total comprehensive income (P&L Rs 180 crore incl. the 12 recycled and ECL 5; OCI +20) equals:
questions.why: TCI = 180 + 20 = 200; the reclassification of 12 from OCI to P&L moves between components but does not change the TCI total (the OCI component for the year nets −12 against +20 ⇒ 200 still).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: TCI = the only place OCI and P&L kiss Recycling shuffles the drawers; the cupboard total is unchanged.

questions.q: Interest paid may be classified under Ind AS 7 in operating or financing activities, whereas dividends PAID are:
questions.why: Ind AS 7 permits interest paid as operating/financing and dividends paid as financing/operating provided consistent classification. (Dividends RECEIVED: investing or operating.)
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 'permitted alternatives' set is a favourite 'except' target AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Four flows, two slots each: int paid O/F; div paid F/O; div received O/I; int received O/I. Consistency beats theory.

questions.q: A company's quick (acid-test) ratio differs from the current ratio mainly because quick ratio excludes:
questions.why: Quick assets = current assets less inventories and usually prepaids; the current ratio counts them.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — definition-level exclusions appear in the analysis chapter as 1-markers AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Acid-test = cash + receivables + listed securities; the warehouse (inventory) and prepaids stay outside.

questions.q: Operating cycle is measured as the time between:
o: Purchase of raw material to cash collection from sales
Payment to suppliers and receipt from customers
questions.why: Operating cycle = inventory days + receivables days; cash conversion = operating cycle less payables days.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — definition freebies in analysis Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Inventory in → cash out of collection = operating cycle; subtract payables' grace for cash conversion.

questions.q: Under the direct method of Ind AS 7, the operating cash flows are shown as:
o: Net profit adjusted for non-cash items
Gross cash receipts from customers and payments to suppliers/employees
questions.why: Direct method presents major classes of gross receipts/payments; indirect method starts from profit and reconciles. Both target the same operating total.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — method-comparison quickie Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 7 — direct vs indirect
mem.tip: Direct = bank-statement view; indirect = P&L-to-cash reconciliation. Only investing/financing stay gross-gross on both? — same figures, different tour.

questions.q: Cash held in foreign currency is reported in the cash flow statement at:
o: Historical exchange rates from the date of incorporation
The exchange rates at the dates of the cash flows (Ind AS 21 rates on those dates)
questions.why: Ind AS 7: foreign currency cash flows are reported at the exchange rate at the dates of the cash flows; the entity's foreign cash balances at closing rate.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the rate-date pairing tests exact recall Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Flows wear their own day's rate; balances wear year-end's. Never borrow the other's coat.

questions.q: High operating leverage with unchanged sales, when EBIT falls, EPS falls:
o: By a larger proportion due to fixed operating costs
questions.why: Combined leverage (DOL×DFL) magnifies EPS moves; with fixed costs and fixed finance, an EBIT fall hits EPS harder than proportionally.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — leverage-layering logic questions Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Fixed at the top and bottom? The middle (EPS) feels every tremor double.

questions.q: Working capital equals:
questions.why: WC = CA − CL; the RATIO version is CA/CL — one subtraction, one division.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — definition pair separation AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Working capital is a balance in rupees; the current ratio is the same idea as a fraction.

questions.q: Cash conversion cycle = inventory days + receivables days − ?
questions.why: CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO; the longer the payables delay, the shorter the cash gap.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — formula-signs questions AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Buy slowly, sell fast: the payables line is the only minus sign.

questions.q: Which ratio most directly measures long-term solvency?
questions.why: Long-term solvency: D/E, interest coverage, proprietary ratio; current and turnover metrics are short-term/efficiency.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — ratio-classification sorting Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Structure ratios look at the mountain (capital), not the ripples (working days).

questions.q: Which is NOT a cash equivalent?
o: Bank overdrafts repayable on demand (as negative cash)
questions.why: Equity investments are excluded (no determinable maturity, variable value) — overdrafts are deducted from cash for cash-flow purposes where repayable on demand.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — exception-lists are cash-flow gold AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Cash equivalents need a short fuse — equity has no expiry date at all.

questions.q: High accruals relative to operating cash flows generally signal:
questions.why: Aggressive accrual accounting vs cash-backed earnings: the gap flags quality risk (a core analytical ratio idea in the new syllabus).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — accruals-vs-cash heuristic AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Profit is opinion, cash is fact — diverge and question the opinion.

questions.q: Proceeds from disposal of a subsidiary are presented in cash flows under:
questions.why: Disposal proceeds: investing (net of cash and equivalents disposed); disclose as a single amount.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the net-of-cash rule AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Cash flow — disposal of subsidiary
mem.tip: When the sub leaves with its cash, only the net cheque is investing.

questions.topic: New syllabus — integrated reporting / six capitals
questions.q: The Analysis of Financial Statements chapter under the new scheme expects familiarity with broader value-creation reporting. The six capitals of the <IR> framework comprise:
o: Cash, gold, FX, equity, debt, tax
Financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social and relationship, natural
questions.why: Syllabus addition/emphasis: integrated-thinking concepts (six capitals, value-creation story) sit in the new scheme's analysis/reporting awareness — a theory MCQ zone, not an Ind AS amendment.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — new vocabulary in new attempts is cheap 1-mark bait Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: New syllabus — integrated reporting / six capitals
mem.tip: Capitals count beyond cash: the firm's whole battery, from people to topsoil.

questions.q: Profit before tax 300; depreciation 90; gain on sale of PPE 30; receivables up 50; inventory up 23; payables up 26 (all Rs lakh). Operating cash flow (indirect method):
questions.why: PBT + 90 − gain 30 − DR 50 − Inv 23 + AP 26 = Rs 313 lakh. Investing gain is stripped (its proceeds live in investing).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — indirect-method assembly with three WC moves is a standard quickie AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Indirect method: PBT + non-cash charges − non-operating gains; working-capital moves per sign.

questions.q: Meridian Ltd recorded an import payable of USD 100,000 at Rs 83/USD (Rs 7 lakh) on 1 January; at year end the rate is Rs 84/USD. The Ind AS 21 treatment is (amounts per Rs 7 lakh base):
o: Exchange gain of Rs 0.07 crore to P&L
Nil — importers are not exposed to exchange risk
Exchange loss of Rs 0.07 crore to P&L (payable restated at Rs 84/USD)
OCI as a foreign currency translation reserve
questions.why: Foreign-currency MONETARY items are retranslated at the closing rate. The rupee weakens from 83 to 84 so the payable rises by Rs 7.0 lakh — an exchange LOSS in P&L (a receivable would give a gain). P&L recognition — OCI translation applies to foreign OPERATIONS, not to individual monetary items.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — monetary-vs-non-monetary retranslation with sign direction is evergreen AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Monetary foreign-currency items at closing rate; exchange differences to P&L (net investment/qualifying hedge exceptions aside).

o: Exchange loss of Rs 0.09 crore to P&L (payable restated at Rs 84/USD)
Exchange gain of Rs 0.09 crore to P&L
Nil — importers are not exposed to exchange risk
OCI as a foreign currency translation reserve
questions.why: Foreign-currency MONETARY items are retranslated at the closing rate. The rupee weakens from 83 to 84 so the payable rises by Rs 9.0 lakh — an exchange LOSS in P&L (a receivable would give a gain). P&L recognition — OCI translation applies to foreign OPERATIONS, not to individual monetary items.
